reviewer.tool: agent image read tool on the captured PNGs listed below; numeric Debug HDR readback

observations: Nine camera-facing quads isolate the authored inputs: a plain baseline, clearcoat factor/roughness/normal maps, specular factor+color maps, sheen color+roughness maps, a transmission map, a UV1 clearcoat map and a KHR_texture_transform clearcoat map.

Every mapped probe changes its effective-lobe diagnostic value between the left and right sample of the same quad: clearcoat R gradient, clearcoat roughness G gradient, coat-normal perturbation, specular A gradient, specular-color RGB gradient, sheen color RGB gradient, sheen roughness A gradient and transmission R gradient.

The plain quad keeps clearcoat 0, sheen 0, transmission 0 and specular F90 1 at both samples; the UV1 clearcoat quad stays at its 0.6 factor because the unsupported set is unbound rather than aliased to UV0.

The specular factor and specular color maps share one authored PNG but report distinct image chunk ids with linear and sRGB color spaces; the left/right specular F0 and F90 values follow the authored gradients.
The transformed clearcoat quad reports offset [0.5,0] and scale [2,1] and its channel-12 gradient is reversed by the transform.

The channel images show the expected separation: clearcoat channels light only the coated probes, the specular-color channel lights only the specular probe, sheen/transmission/coat-normal channels stay on their own probes, and the baseline stays black.

After one injected device removal the viewer rebuilds the device from the retained source and all nine draw records return with the authored extension maps bound; the post-reset capture is not fallback grey.
The generated fixture opens with the expected first-open framing in Studio; no new clipping or washout is visible.

defects.label: limitation
defects.description: Transmission still uses the alpha-carried interface Fresnel and no transmitted-scene sampling. Channel 28 verifies the per-texel transmission factor itself; T26/T27 own the physical path.

defects.label: limitation
defects.description: KHR_materials_volume, anisotropy, iridescence and dispersion remain parsed-but-unrendered with specific compatibility records. T25 claims only clearcoat/specular/sheen/transmission map paths.

defects.label: limitation
defects.description: The normalized vertex layouts still carry only TEXCOORD_0, so an authored UV1 map stays unbound with kTextureFeatureUnsupportedUvSet. It is not sampled against UV0.

positives: Wire v14 remains a fixed closed record: thirteen material slots, sixteen dependency ids, no variable-length per-material binding list.
The textured root signature is 44 of 64 DWORDs; the per-material CBV stays a bounded 1024-byte stride and no per-slot data became root constants.
Unbound slots bind neutral descriptors and the map mask skips them; an authored map is never reported as resident when only a fallback is bound.
Import, wire-validator, hostile-worker, texture-budget, coarse/detail, texture-decode and cache lanes all pass in the T25 serial set.
Release still rejects every test-control message; the new fields/channels remain inside the Debug --app-smoke guard.

acceptance.acceptedReferencesPromotedBy: not applicable for T25 (observed evidence only)
acceptance.note: Reviewed the T25-dev run generated by the same profile/binary; the final T25 run writes the identical paths listed above. No baseline or reference was promoted.
